$comment: Enumerated record-bearing classes that no shape targets, for scripts/check-class-coverage.py. This file is a GATE INPUT, not a filter: the check still examines and counts every class declaring rdfs:subClassOf prov:Entity or prov:Activity. The run fails when an unshaped class appears that is not listed here AND when a listed class stops being unshaped, so the list can only shrink, and shrinking it is an explicit committed edit. Each entry names the vocabulary that owns the fix. Nothing here is acceptable in the long run -- each entry is a class whose records SHACL reports conforms:true over while having examined nothing, a verdict indistinguishable from one that was earned.
$rule: A class declaring rdfs:subClassOf prov:Entity or prov:Activity has said its instances are record data. If no shape names it in sh:targetClass then those records are judged by nothing. The cure is a shape with an explicit sh:targetClass -- never a subclass axiom, which SHACL does not resolve over a pod's data graph (see validation/index.md). Where a class turns out NOT to hold record data, the cure is instead to reconsider the PROV superclass, which is the thing declaring that it does.
$established: 2026-08-30, clinical v1.18 (spec). clinical:CoverageRecord, the class this check was written for, is FIXED rather than baselined: it is shaped by clinical:CoverageRecordShape in the same change. The regression suite deletes that shape from a scratch copy and requires the check to name the class, which is what proves this would have caught it.

entries.detail: PROBABLY THE SUPERCLASS, NOT THE SHAPE. This is the classification whose INDIVIDUALS are cascade:ClinicalGenerated, cascade:EHRVerified, cascade:PatientReported and the rest; no pod record is ever typed cascade:DataProvenance, so there is nothing for a shape to judge. Its rdfs:subClassOf prov:Entity is what puts it in this check's population and is the declaration worth revisiting. Resolve it one way or the other rather than shaping it: a shape targeting a value enumeration would be the wrong fix.
